articles.title: ‘Super proud’ De Minaur takes down new world No 1 Zverev to reach Vienna Open final
articles.summary: World No 10 holds nerve in 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 (7-4) semi-final win. Australian will meet Carlos Alcaraz in championship match. Alex de Minaur has held his nerve to claim what could be one of the most significant wins of his career, downing the world No 1-elect Alexander Zverev with a fearless display of…
body: The Australian played a fabulous deciding tiebreaker, nervelessly brushing off a couple of double faults to keep the pressure on the two-time grand slam champion to prevail 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 (7-4) to set up a championship match with Carlos Alcaraz at the Wiener Stadthalle.

Saturday’s victory had extra importance because it pushed De Minaur back among the top-eight qualifiers to make the end-of-season men’s championship, the ATP Finals, with next week’s Paris Masters the last qualifying event in the “Race to Turin'’.

The win will also resonate as one of De Minaur’s biggest as he had never previously beaten Zverev in an individual tournament, his only previous victories coming in early-season teams events and the exhibition that is the Laver Cup.

“I’m super proud, super stoked of how I handled the moment. I was very calm, even though I threw in a couple of doubles there,” De Minaur said, pondering how he fought to regain control after his dazzling first set was followed by his serve faltering in the second.

articles.title: Antonelli feeling 'tense' amid effort to seal F1 title
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli has admitted to feeling "more tense than usual" ahead of attempting to seal the Formula 1 world championship at Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix.
body: The 20-year-old only needs to finish ninth in the race to become the sport's youngest world champion.
Antonelli qualified fifth on Saturday but will start from fourth on the grid due to a penalty for Max Verstappen.
Speaking after the session, the Italian revealed that he is not feeling his best as he continues to recover from an illness that caused him to miss his media duties on Thursday.
He told Sky Sports F1: "It has not been the easiest weekend to be fair.

articles.title: Canelo Álvarez wins back world title as Houthi attacks cast shadow over Riyadh
articles.summary: Mexican star wins unanimous decision over Mbilli. Álvarez, 36, regains WBC title after Crawford defeat. Read Bryan Armen Graham’s round-by-round report. Mexico’s Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez reclaimed the WBC super-middleweight title with a unanimous-decision victory over the previously unbeaten Christian…
body: The fight went ahead at Kingdom Arena despite a week of heightened security concerns in the Saudi capital, where the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted missiles and drones launched by Iran-aligned Houthi forces. Several events in the kingdom were cancelled or postponed, including the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition.

Álvarez, 36, fighting for the first time in more than a year, relied on his trademark counter-punching and precise body shots to overcome the aggressive French champion and re-establish himself among boxing’s elite.

“It’s something unbelievable. It feels like my first title. Now, after 21 years as a professional, 16 years ago I won my first title. Now I won that title again. I’m so proud of my team,” ‌Canelo said in English.
“I love boxing. That’s why I’m here, because I still love boxing and I enjoy it a lot.”

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton storms to his first Ferrari pole at F1 Mexican GP with Antonelli fourth
articles.summary: George Russell second on grid after qualifying. Antonelli well placed as he nears title confirmation. Even as Formula One’s young gun Kimi Antonelli remains on course to claim his first world championship on Sunday it was the veteran, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton who gave a salutary reminder…
body: Hamilton delivered a superb lap for Ferrari to secure his first pole for the team and just beat Mercedes’ George Russell into second. World champion in waiting Antonelli was in fourth place but remains in position to close out the title on Sunday, although Hamilton and Russell, who must win the race to have any hope of keeping the fight alive, have at least locked out the front row.

It was clearly a hugely emotional moment for Hamilton at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez to finally nail the top spot for Ferrari in his second season with the team, with the 41-year-old’s 105th pole also his first since 2023.
“Thank you so much, that’s been such a long time coming,” he said. “That feels good. I’m lost for words. My first pole with Ferrari. 105 poles, I like that number.

“Where there’s a will, there’s a way. It’s all in the mind. For sure, you might feel aches and pains, luckily I don’t, I do all those different things to keep myself young and fit. But I love what I do, and love is not gone.”

articles.title: Hamilton: A 'dream' to emulate Schumacher with first Ferrari pole
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton said he had achieved his "dream" of emulating Michael Schumacher after claiming his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
body: The 41-year-old unexpectedly snatched pole from Mercedes' George Russell in a thrilling end to qualifying to take his first pole in over three years and extend his record career pole tally to 105.

Hamilton and Schumacher share the sport's record for the most Drivers' Championships with seven each, but while the Brit won one title with McLaren and the other six with Mercedes, the bulk of Schumacher's success came at Ferrari as he won five in a row from 2000 to 2004.
"It was a dream my family have shared with me and I know so many people in the world grew up watching Michael.
"To be at this point of my career and still have this special feeling - 105 [poles], the number doesn't mean much in a sense, it feels like the first.

articles.title: Hamilton claims first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City GP
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton claimed his first pole position for Ferrari by edging out Mercedes' George Russell in qualifying for the Mexico City Grand Prix.
body: Hamilton had been outpaced by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc throughout the weekend but the 41-year-old produced his best lap when it mattered most at the end of Q3 to edge out Russell by nine thousandths of a second.

The seven-time world champion has twice claimed Sprint poles since his move from Mercedes to Ferrari at the start of the 2025 season but will now start a grand prix from the front of the grid for the first time since July 2023 after extending his record tally to 105 poles.
Speaking over team radio after being confirmed as Formula 1's oldest pole-sitter for 44 years, Hamilton said: "Thank you so much, it has been such a long time coming."
Leclerc had led Max Verstappen after the first runs in Q3, but the pair had to settle for third and fourth, respectively, after both making errors on their final efforts.

articles.title: Ocon denies reports of physical altercation behind dropping
articles.summary: Esteban Ocon denies reports that his being dropped by Haas at the Mexico City Grand Prix was a consequence of a row with team principal Ayao Komatsu descending into a physical confrontation.
body: The Frenchman, 30, admitted in a statement on social media that "a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved".
But he said he "categorically rejected any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve any differences of any nature".
His statement followed a report in France's L'Equipe, external which said that a meeting between Komatsu and Ocon "ended abruptly, perhaps even physically".
The decision to stand Ocon down from the rest of the Mexico weekend came after he had had a dispute with race engineer Laura Mueller about tyre choice during second practice on Friday.

articles.title: Anfernee Simons hits bench scoring mark not seen since 2024
articles.summary: Anfernee Simons hits bench scoring mark not seen since 2024 appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The Philadelphia 76ers might have added star power this offseason, but to win a championship, they’re going to need consistent depth and production…
body: In the 76ers’ win, Anfernee Simons became the first NBA bench player since Malik Beasley in 2024 to have made five or more 3-pointers in three consecutive games. Against the Hornets, Simons hit five 3-pointers in nine attempts (55.5 percent). He finished with 19 points, two assists and three steals in 25 minutes of play.

Simons signed with the 76ers in the offseason via free agency after splitting last season between the Boston Celtics and Chicago Bulls. Through the 76ers’ first six games of the season, he’s been a big part of why they started out 5-1 coming into the game against the Hornets.

He had played in all six games coming into Saturday’s matchup, at a little over 24 minutes per game. He was averaging 10.8 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists with splits of 41.5 percent shooting from the field, 41 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 71.4 percent shooting from the free-throw line.

The No. 24 overall pick in the 2018 NBA Draft, Simons began his career with the Portland Trail Blazers. He played the first seven seasons of his career with the Blazers before being included in a trade with the Celtics in the same deal that brought Jrue Holiday to Portland.

articles.title: What Cincinnati coach Scott Satterfield said after losing to Utah
articles.summary: For Cincinnati fans, Halloween got off to a rough start after the Bearcats were dominated dominant 49-25 by the Utah Utes at Nippert Stadium. After being scored on by Utah on the first drive of the game, the Bearcats responded with a field goal, but that was as close as the margin got as Utah’s…
body: “Obviously, we knew Utah was a good football team coming in, and they certainly played like it there in the first half,” Bearcats coach Scott Satterfield said.

“We didn’t help ourselves at all. We were able to move the football a little bit, and you get down, and then we shot ourselves in the foot with a couple penalties that knocked us out. We knew going into it, if you get an opportunity, when you get down close to the goal line, you gotta punch it in and get touchdowns.”
Touchdowns were not something Cincinnati was good at getting in the first half, as the Bearcats only scored the two field goals. The Utes were simply too much on both sides of the ball.

“We did a poor job tackling on the perimeter, allowing them to get some chunk plays and chunk yards, and when you do that, you open up the middle a little bit, and all of a sudden they’re powerful enough and fast enough to get yards up the middle,” Satterfield said.

articles.title: Suzuki makes string of saves before conceding own goal in draw with Fulham
articles.summary: Nicolas Jackson scored his eighth goal in 10 games but an error from goalkeeper Zion Suzuki meant Aston Villa had to settle for a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham.
body: Villa should have gone ahead after 15 minutes when they were awarded a penalty following a review when Sander Berge was penalised for a handball in the box as he jumped with Leon Goretzka at a corner.

With neither Emi Buendia nor Ross Barkley in the line-up, John McGinn stepped up to take the penalty but the Scotland international - who had only ever taken a penalty for Villa in a shoot-out - smashed the ball against the crossbar and over.

The home side nearly paid a heavy price for McGinn's miss straightaway after a Fulham counter-attack, but Oscar Bobb was brilliantly denied the opener by a one-handed save from Suzuki who tipped the ball over.

Villa went in front after Timothy Castagne's error allowed Johan Manzambi to play a ball through to Jackson, who cut inside and beat David Affengruber, before wriggling clear of the recovering Castagne to slide the ball past Bernd Leno.

articles.title: The WNBA Finals were decided by an all-time performance
articles.summary: Gabby Williams had just two points at halftime in the Golden State Valkyries’ Game 7 against the Atlanta Dream. The Valkyries trailed the Dream by 6 and, once again, struggled offensively. But Williams went off in the third quarter, pouring in three consecutive triples and 15 points in the period.
body: “Man, I don’t know,” Williams said in her walkoff interview. “I love moments like this. Nat told me to be patient in the first half — it was hard, but I listened, and she was right as always.”
The Valkyries trailed by as many as 9 points in the third quarter when Williams caught fire, scoring 11 points in a two-minute span to give the Valkyries a 1-point lead entering the fourth quarter.
Williams, whom Valkyries owner Joe Lacob proclaimed was the best player in the world in the first round of the playoffs, looked like it when it mattered most.

During the season, Williams averaged 14.4 points and 2.2 assists per game. But in the postseason, she elevated her game, averaging 20.3 points and 3.4 assists per game entering the decisive Game 7. Williams recorded 26 points in Games 1 and 6 of the Finals, but she saved her best performance for last.
